verdict_vs_market.quote: This is a fair offer, but it isn't a strong reason to leave a job you're happy in.

verdict_vs_current.quote: Against your $526K at Meta, that's about $26K more, or roughly 5%.

recommendation.quote: Negotiate. Don't accept as-is, and don't walk away yet.

equity_grounding.quote: Tie the ask to the Meta stock you'd give up and the refresh pipeline you'd have to rebuild.

uses_general_market_benchmark.quote: Similar L6 roles in the Bay Area show median pay around $485,400 (product design managers), so this offer seems at or above market.

refresh_valued_at.quote: years 3–4 drop well below what you make now unless refreshes fill the gap.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: Walk away if Google won't move from about 5%. Staying where you're happy, with your refresh pipeline intact, is worth more than $26K a year.

unsupported_claims.claim: Stock is usually where Google has the most room to move
unsupported_claims.quote: Stock: this is usually where Google has the most room to move.

unsupported_claims.claim: Recruiters can approve sign-on bonuses more easily than base increases
unsupported_claims.quote: Recruiters can usually approve this more easily than base increases.

missing_info_requested: Exact vesting schedule for the new-hire grant
Timing and vesting of the first refresh grant
Start date flexibility around Meta bonus payout

ask_focus.quote: To get me to yes, I'd need a base of $262K, a new-hire grant of $1.4M and a $100K sign-on bonus.

rsu_annualized.quote: Average per year over 4 years: $235K base + $47K bonus + $270K stock = about $552K.

year1_vs_recurring.quote: roughly 17–20% above Meta, plus a one-time sign-on.

forfeiture_as_loss.quote: Leaving Meta before its annual bonus pays out could cost you that year's ~$36K. Leaving before refresh season means giving up that grant too.
